Lesson 8.4 · 18 min · Verified 17 Jul 2026

Product families: how policy changes with the product

After this lesson you can:
  • Tour India's retail/MSME product families and their distinguishing controls
  • Map product differences to policy, collateral and schedule variations
  • Know what LoanOS's first slice supports versus catalogues
On this page
  1. The same skeleton, different organs
  2. What a BA extracts from this
  3. Where this lives in LoanOS
  4. Knowledge check

1. The same skeleton, different organs

Every product this platform catalogues walks the same lifecycle you have learned — consent, KYC, decision, KFS, disbursement, servicing, collections, closure. What changes per family is the policy, collateral and schedule shape:

  • Unsecured personal term loan — the baseline this course traced; FOIR-led decisioning, monthly EMI, no collateral. LoanOS's first-slice depth is here.
  • MSME term loan — business income analysis (GST returns, ITR, bank cash flows via AA), Udyam registration, sometimes CGTMSE guarantee cover in place of collateral.
  • Working capital / OD / cash credit — revolving limits, daily-reducing interest, utilisation and limit reviews rather than fixed EMIs.
  • Home loan / LAP — property collateral: title opinion, valuation, LTV caps, CERSAI registration, construction-linked tranche disbursement; the longest tenors.
  • Vehicle / equipment finance — asset-backed with RTO/registry lien, dealer/end-use payment at disbursement, repossession as the recovery lever.
  • Gold loan — LTV-regulated against pledged gold, short tenors, bullet or interest-serviced schedules, auction as recovery.
  • Education loan — moratorium through study plus grace, step-up repayment.
  • Agri / seasonal — harvest-aligned irregular schedules, PSL classification relevance.
  • Supply-chain / invoice finance — receivable-backed, tenor tied to invoice maturity.

2. What a BA extracts from this

When scoping a new product, interrogate the family: What secures it (and which registry perfects it)?

What schedule shape fits the cash flows?

Which extra verifications enter KYC/underwriting (property title, dealer invoice, gold assay, Udyam)?

Which recovery levers apply (SARFAESI needs security interest; repossession needs the asset)?

Which regulatory overlays attach (LTV caps, PSL tags, MFI rules — noting the platform currently excludes JLG/MFI-specific machinery)?

Each answer lands in the same place: an effective-dated product policy with its eligibility, pricing, schedule and document requirements — module 3's policy-as-data, parameterised per family. The capability catalogue's product packs enumerate exactly which capabilities each family needs beyond the core.

Regulatory anchors

  • RBI-DL-2025 — Digital lending conduct applies across product families.
  • CERSAI-CKYC — Secured families ride on registry perfection (CERSAI, RTO, land records).

Family IDs resolve in the India regulatory register (docs/compliance/india-regulatory-register.md), which owns sources and caveats.

Where this lives in LoanOS

  • Document docs/product/complete-system-capability-catalog.md — Product-specific capability packs: per-family requirements beyond the core.
  • Capability COL-006 — LTV, margin, haircut and revaluation policy for secured families.
  • Capability LMS-008 — Revolving credit, OD, cash credit and drawdown facilities.
  • Operating guide configure-product (open in the Guide) — Operating guide: configure a lending product policy.

Key terms

FOIR SARFAESI CERSAI Moratorium AA

Knowledge check

1. Which product family most naturally uses a bullet repayment schedule?

  1. Salaried personal loan
  2. Home loan
  3. Gold loan
  4. Education loan
Show answer

C. Short-tenor gold loans commonly repay principal at maturity (bullet), with the pledged gold securing the exposure.

2. What must exist before SARFAESI can be used on a home loan default?

  1. A guarantor
  2. A registered security interest (e.g. CERSAI) and NPA status
  3. A court decree
  4. DLG cover
Show answer

B. SARFAESI enforcement requires a perfected security interest and applies to NPA accounts — no decree needed, that being its point.
